clue.text: Possibly infer that French conservationists find this rare

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word infer may be rearranged into another order

parts.note: que is French for that
NT is the National Trust, Britain's heritage conservation body

explanation.surface: A guess that French conservation workers hardly ever find this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' reorders the five letters of 'infer'; the National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens seldom is uncommon, which is what rare means.

clue.text: Well-nigh niggardly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means almost (near enough) and also tight-fisted, as in a near person who won't spend.

clue.text: Advert about English jacket

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: An advertisement promoting an English-made coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' is the verb (to allude), not an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket of the kind worn by sailors.

clue.text: Missile that's a bone of contention?

definitions.meaning: a short heavy bolt shot from a crossbow
a subject of dispute, an argument

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a crossbow bolt and a row or dispute between people.

clue.text: The artist is in general a quiet type

indicators.note: is in tells us the name sits inside the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Painters are generally retiring sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was an English painter of nudes; his name runs across 'quiet type'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty (1787-1849) was a York-born painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: A hill-dwelling six-footer

parts.note: a six-footer sounds like a tall person, but means a six-legged insect living in a mound

explanation.surface: A tall person living up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Insects have six feet, and these ones build great earth mounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect has six legs and lives in a colony that builds a tall earthen mound.

clue.text: Issue raised by a gold prospector

definitions.text: Issue raised by a gold prospector

parts.words: Issue raised by a gold prospector
parts.note: issue means offspring: the daughter of the miner forty-niner in the old American song

explanation.surface: A complaint put forward by a man panning for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In the American folk song 'Oh My Darling', the girl is the daughter of a miner, a forty-niner in the California gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine is the child the prospector brought up.

clue.text: Once favoured by women appreciating a good spread!

definitions.text: Once favoured by women appreciating a good spread!

parts.words: Once favoured by women appreciating a good spread!
parts.note: a good spread sounds like a feast, but means the wide flare of a Victorian skirt on its hooped frame

explanation.surface: Something women used to love when they enjoyed a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests a meal; here it is the width of a hooped petticoat.
explanation.definitionFit: These stiffened hooped petticoats, fashionable in the mid-1800s, made skirts stand out wide.

clue.text: Don't speak out clearly when making an aspersion

definitions.meaning: a slight or insult on someone's character

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to mumble words together and also a slanderous remark.

clue.text: Criminal fellow, the commission-agent!.

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male
a factor is an agent who buys and sells for others on commission

explanation.surface: A crook of a man: the middleman taking a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, someone who commits a crime, is a malefactor.

clue.text: Putting many a decoration on to show worldly wealth

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so it stands for many
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wearing medals to flaunt how rich one is.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Medal is a British gallantry award, abbreviated MM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammon is riches personified as an idol in the Bible, material gain.

clue.text: Clarets may well be a very bright red

indicators.note: may well be suggests the letters of clarets could become something else when reordered

explanation.surface: Red wines can turn out a vivid crimson.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant shade of red, brighter than crimson.

clue.text: Bad night? A rest may be arranged if cracking up

indicators.note: bad suggests the word night is spoilt and jumbled
may be arranged tells us these letters can be put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: After a sleepless night, some rest can be organised if one is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' and 'may be arranged' both act on NIGHT plus A REST, mixed as one pool of ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering means breaking into pieces, as something cracking up does.

clue.text: One wrapping soft fruit with an air

indicators.note: wrapping means one piece goes around the others like a cover

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
P is piano, the musical direction for soft
a pear is a fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone covering a delicate fruit with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is a playing card here, and 'soft' is the musical marking piano; 'with an air' looks like a manner but 'an' is fodder and 'air' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or look someone gives off, their outward look.

clue.text: Course taken by a singer

definitions.meaning: the general drift or direction, as in the course of events

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the general direction something takes and also a high male voice part.

clue.text: Oriental flier, a trainee, going on and on

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
a tern is a seabird, so a flier
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: An Eastern bird and a novice keep going endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner: British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting goes on without end.

clue.text: Two characters getting together in a German town

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
en is the spelt-out name of the letter N

explanation.surface: Two people meeting up in a town in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters are letters: the names of S and N are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, western Germany.

clue.text: Become tenants-like being in sheltered accommodation

indicators.note: being in means this word sits inside the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind
as means like, as in fit as a fiddle

explanation.surface: Becoming renters, like people living in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheltered accommodation' looks like housing for the elderly but just means a lee, a sheltered place.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a property on a rental contract is to hold it as a tenant.

clue.text: How a politician's power is rated?

definitions.text: How a politician's power is rated?

parts.words: How a politician's power is rated?
parts.note: read as a unit for electric current, also as a member of parliament, with an article before

explanation.surface: How an MP's influence is measured.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MP'S read together gives the unit of electric current, used to rate electrical appliances.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical equipment is rated by the current it draws, measured in units named after Ampère.

clue.text: The beast will be left with one over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
on can mean over, as a lid is on or over a pot

explanation.surface: The animal will be abandoned with one more remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is the big cat known as king of beasts.

clue.text: Building quarters within a great rock

indicators.note: within shows one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a tor is a high rocky outcrop, as on Dartmoor
W and E are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Constructing living quarters inside a huge rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop found on English moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower is a tall building or structure.

clue.text: Housing suggestion offered without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a trace is a hint or suggestion
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: Accommodation offered straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' looks like 'promptly', but 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the hint goes round the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, a form of housing.

clue.text: Manage grain production in the North-west

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
corn is cereal grain produced on farms

explanation.surface: Running cereal farming in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Runcorn is an industrial town in Cheshire, in North-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is a town on the Mersey in Cheshire, a place in that region of England.

clue.text: Cheer at the trainer's discomposure

indicators.note: discomposure means being thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Applause at the coach's embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach or instructor trains people, as one who teaches does.

clue.text: Pain-killers for tots

definitions.meaning: things that numb, that deaden feeling

explanation.definitionFit: Read as things that numb, the word is anaesthetics; read normally, it is figures one totals up.

clue.text: The poet's penniless, having received nothing

indicators.note: having received means the word takes in another one

parts.note: broke means having no money
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The writer is broke and got nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke was an English war poet who wrote 'The Soldier'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke (1887-1915) wrote famous First World War sonnets, so he was a poet.

clue.text: Thatcher's sound as a lecturer!

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a reeder is a thatcher, one who roofs with reeds

explanation.surface: The noise made by Margaret Thatcher as a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' suggests the prime minister, but it is a roofer working in reeds; Reader is a senior British university lecturing rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a Reader is a senior lecturer just below professor.

clue.text: Boss providing stable employment

definitions.meaning: a stable used for breeding horses

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a raised ornamental knob and also an establishment where horses are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Only requiring a couple of notes

parts.note: me is the third note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Needing just two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means just or nothing more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: The scientist rents a room for working

indicators.note: working signals the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: The researcher lets out a room to earn money.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies stars and planets, a kind of scientist.

clue.text: Delightful as a holiday resort

explanation.definitionFit: The word means pleasant, and also names the Riviera resort city in France.

clue.text: Put in a difficult position when a tip gave offence

parts.note: an end is a tip or extremity
angered means made cross, gave offence

explanation.surface: Upset when a gratuity caused annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a gratuity, but it is the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To place in danger or a precarious situation is to threaten, to imperil.
